pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-N-Methyl-D-Aspartate Receptor (Anti-NMDAR) Encephalitis secondary to an Ovarian Teratoma THE SMOKING GUN: The electroencephalogram showing an "extreme delta brush" pattern paired with stereotypic orofacial dyskinesias, catatonia, autonomic instability, and an occult mature cystic teratoma detected on pelvic transvaginal ultrasound. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: This autoimmune encephalitis is driven by pathogenic IgG antibodies directed against the GluN1 (NR1) subunit of the NMDA receptor. The process is frequently paraneoplastic, initiated when ectopic neural tissue inside a neoplasm (predominantly an ovarian dermoid/teratoma in young women) exposes NMDA receptors to systemic immune surveillance. The resulting autoantibodies cross the blood-brain barrier and bind to neuronal cell surfaces, causing antibody-mediated cross-linking and selective endocytosis (internalization) of surface NMDA receptors. The profound depletion of these receptors in forebrain and hippocampal pathways abolishes inhibitory GABAergic interneuron transmission. This unchecked disinhibition precipitates severe frontostriatal and limbic overdrive, generating acute psychosis, catatonia, bizarre involuntary movement disorders, autonomic storming, and central hypoventilation. Prompt tumor resection and aggressive immunotherapy (corticosteroids, IVIG, or plasmapheresis) are critical to reversing receptor downregulation and avoiding fatality.
